question: Can a class-balanced, CV-tuned gradient-boosting model that uses STL-style window features match or beat a neural sequence baseline at labelling signals with a known temporal logic formula, and does it do so more stably across seeds?
method: Seeded random-walk signals (length 100) labelled by the fixed STL formula 'eventually in [0,20] x>0.6 and always in [0,50] x<0.95'. Per seed: one stratified train/test split; CV grid search on train only; test scored once.

dataset.name: Simulated random-walk signals with exact STL labels

baseline: sklearn MLPClassifier on the raw 100-point signal (StandardScaler), grid over learning rate and hidden size chosen by 3-fold CV; stands in for the paper's recurrent network.
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM on sliding-window max/min/mean and threshold-crossing-time features plus formula-horizon prefix extrema; grid over num_leaves and learning rate chosen by 3-fold CV.
notes: Simulated data only, so results do not transfer to the paper's own benchmark. Only 3 seeds and small grids; std is across seeds. The formula is fixed and known, which favours hand-crafted window features. Macro-F1 is a secondary metric. Per-seed positive rate is printed in the log.
